$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =ax \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 8 \\ 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =3\cdot (-5)+0\cdot 8+4\cdot 5 \\  & =-15+0+20 \\  & =5.\end{aligned}
$$" :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186161981 :knowledge-point/questions ["question-8fd187ae-a269-5381-90d7-f0ba2d5b4ded" "question-bc56657a-b79e-53ee-87cf-34f486cb39d6"] :db/ensure [:knowledge-point/validate]} {:db/id 17592186161773 :question/problem "Consider the the bilinear form $B(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y}),$ given by 

$$
B(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y})= 2 x_1y_2 - x_2y_2 +3 x_2y_3-x_3y_1
$$

 

Evaluate $B(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y})$ when ![](images/e3/e355ba8664f980f8e06bcbda40adf063d376478e745b9b6b036331a895192c54.svg) and ![](images/7f/7fe125bd6366adb85e10ab5719049e1e0db7c719b4a714f9155efee77a8f604b.svg)" :question/worked-solution "We are given that 

$\qquad$ ![](images/14/14418dfa570c1be7015799f009ad93388a6dd6d04bed48972bc8163351bbeb87.svg) and ![](images/8b/8bc4748c7c554dc1edfbdce567f9e6d994ebe0955346bfa34712e20286aaa3b3.svg) 

Substituting these into the bilinear expression, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}B(x,y) & =2{x}_{1}{y}_{2}-{x}_{2}{y}_{2}+3{x}_{2}{y}_{3}-{x}_{3}{y}_{1} \\  & =2\cdot 1\cdot 2-1\cdot 2+3\cdot 1\cdot 1-(-1)\cdot (-2) \\  & =4-2+3-2 \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$" :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186161982 :knowledge-point/questions ["question-b15d4431-e43f-5101-96e7-ab09f0076b4a" "question-8f253585-3e9e-576c-84e8-68a00302ab3a"] :db/ensure [:knowledge-point/validate]} {:db/id 17592186161774 :question/problem "![](images/75/7505a6fdbe31e7e3e35e1b9b393d04753b0ccd534e5bacda199e8fc902a5fe3c.svg)
Consider the matrix ![](images/32/3207697e43e4f88223ad85c16964c3103a50c0c999a4ca14417695158d45526b.svg) above.  Write down a bilinear form ![](images/50/50fa4bc1260a734d8f2a1c3045c81dd58e5148d81b6bd85e901c492ab4f61ead.svg) in terms of the components of ![](images/2c/2c28ae197ea4a26ad524d5e6cc89a18a21bf6f215b14432d5377fb3c8a287b6f.svg) and ![](images/35/356a4d35d556458edf899d2b0a49d6db2d47743c0d029c58e1bd3a3b88d9b8c9.svg)" :question/worked-solution "**Method 1**

Each entry ![](images/b6/b6e5dec69a4614a003b3e1e77d18dfb6747cf556fa6f1374803ab0ffc765a3cb.svg) of ![](images/32/3207697e43e4f88223ad85c16964c3103a50c0c999a4ca14417695158d45526b.svg) corresponds to the term ![](images/6e/6e2dccb072d3420de2a0d2d4c9ad9b3f3ff44f62a59c0b3580ced4cdc42f9c9e.svg) in the expression of the bilinear form:

![](images/c3/c3b74ef5a2e970298bd4117c499d18a7bc3319c5e4d4c05b83e0e25fb18fba30.svg)

**Method 2**

To write down a bilinear form in terms of vector components, we compute the following expression:

![](images/aa/aa4630ec70bc3741e32a93d26aa15090e187b8e660ce611bc80e20e2bd8114e8.svg)" :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186161983 :knowledge-point/questions ["question-a33de8e7-0315-5081-b30e-a76239172d51" "question-41f16b5c-e680-54f8-926b-ebe6345d8561"] :db/ensure [:knowledge-point/validate]} {:db/id 17592186161775 :question/worked-solution "Each term $a_{ij}x_i y_j$ in the expression of the bilinear form corresponds to the entry $a_{ij}$ of the matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned}B(x,y) & =2{x}_{1}{y}_{1}+2{x}_{2}{y}_{1}-{x}_{3}{y}_{2}+2{x}_{3}{y}_{3} \\  & =2{x}_{1}{y}_{1}+0{x}_{1}{y}_{2}+0{x}_{1}{y}_{3} \\  & +\,2{x}_{2}{y}_{1}+0{x}_{2}{y}_{2}+0{x}_{2}{y}_{3} \\  & +\,0{x}_{3}{y}_{1}+(-1){x}_{3}{y}_{2}+2{x}_{3}{y}_{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, the corresponding matrix of the bilinear form is

![](images/44/443b1cf1d4425f83b834101627dd202732cf2c905848c8ddbb93dd518f3b35db.svg)

Therefore, $a=2,$ $b=2,$ and $c=-1.$ Finally, 

$$
a+b+c=2+2+(-1) = 3.
$$" :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "question-6cffcafb-88aa-554a-9e0e-d0b676da85d1" :question/id #uuid "6cffcafb-88aa-554a-9e0e-d0b676da85d1" :question/math-academy-id "q-93906" :question/problem "The linear form $f(x)$ is defined as $f(x)=ax,$ where $a=[\begin{aligned}5 & 2 & -3 & 2\end{aligned}].$  Evaluate the function when $x=[\begin{aligned}\,\,2 \\ -4 \\ \,\,1 \\ \,2\end{aligned}].$" :question/worked-solution "Substituting $x=[\begin{aligned}\,\,2 \\ -4 \\ \,\,1 \\ \,2\end{aligned}],$ we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =ax \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5 & 2 & -3 & 2\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}\,\,2 \\ -4 \\ \,\,1 \\ \,2\end{aligned}] \\  & =5\cdot 2+2\cdot (-4)+(-3)\cdot 1+2\cdot 2 \\  & =10-8-3+4 \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-25010ff5-ab1c-5a8c-a044-e8048ed684a5"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}]
$$

Given the matrix $A$ above, evaluate the bilinear form $B(x,y)={x}^{T}\,Ay$ when $x=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ and $y=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$" :question/worked-solution "Substituting $x=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ and $y=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{aligned}],$ we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}B(x,y) & ={x}^{T}\,Ay \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-d1fd5e82-7e1e-5e80-89d9-fc63ac2ef995"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-d1fd5e82-7e1e-5e80-89d9-fc63ac2ef995" :answer-field/id #uuid "d1fd5e82-7e1e-5e80-89d9-fc63ac2ef995" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/radio :answer-field/correct "answer-afe1c099-4476-5cd6-8168-bb6f44c3c646" :answer-field/choices ["answer-c2701e16-efe4-5b21-b6fa-6619278a33a6" "answer-afe1c099-4476-5cd6-8168-bb6f44c3c646" "answer-eccf2580-037b-52f5-a74d-d1ddb3539839" "answer-2cff8026-19f3-5d12-8d4a-fdebbba7f5dc" "answer-7b78cc5b-5be7-561b-961d-acbfeed38058"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-c2701e16-efe4-5b21-b6fa-6619278a33a6" :answer/id #uuid "c2701e16-efe4-5b21-b6fa-6619278a33a6" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "-6" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-afe1c099-4476-5cd6-8168-bb6f44c3c646" :answer/id #uuid "afe1c099-4476-5cd6-8168-bb6f44c3c646" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "4" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-eccf2580-037b-52f5-a74d-d1ddb3539839" :answer/id #uuid "eccf2580-037b-52f5-a74d-d1ddb3539839" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "6" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-2cff8026-19f3-5d12-8d4a-fdebbba7f5dc" :answer/id #uuid "2cff8026-19f3-5d12-8d4a-fdebbba7f5dc" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "8" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-7b78cc5b-5be7-561b-961d-acbfeed38058" :answer/id #uuid "7b78cc5b-5be7-561b-961d-acbfeed38058" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "9" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "question-bc56657a-b79e-53ee-87cf-34f486cb39d6" :question/id #uuid "bc56657a-b79e-53ee-87cf-34f486cb39d6" :question/math-academy-id "q-93920" :question/problem "Consider the bilinear form $B(x,y),$ given by 

$$
B(x,y)={x}_{1}{y}_{1}-2{x}_{1}{y}_{2}+{x}_{1}{y}_{3}-{x}_{2}{y}_{2}+{x}_{3}{y}_{1}.
$$

 

Evaluate $B(x,y)$ when $x=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]$ and $y=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$" :question/worked-solution "We are given that 

$\,$ $x=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,y=[\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2} \\ {y}_{3}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$

Substituting these into the bilinear expression, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}B(x,y) & ={x}_{1}{y}_{1}-2{x}_{1}{y}_{2}+{x}_{1}{y}_{3}-{x}_{2}{y}_{2}+{x}_{3}{y}_{1}. \\  & =0\cdot 2-2\cdot 0\cdot 1+0\cdot 2-1\cdot 1+(-1)\cdot 2 \\  & =0-0+0-1-2 \\  & =-3.\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-4bb5e8f5-c9f7-536e-9428-9ca34ec2e366"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-4bb5e8f5-c9f7-536e-9428-9ca34ec2e366" :answer-field/id #uuid "4bb5e8f5-c9f7-536e-9428-9ca34ec2e366" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/radio :answer-field/correct "answer-16d0649e-68ce-5666-85e2-10cd035eb702" :answer-field/choices ["answer-16d0649e-68ce-5666-85e2-10cd035eb702" "answer-4c939ced-410b-538a-b95e-7eabbbc8766a" "answer-21bd4957-61ca-515f-955c-429ec430a2c2" "answer-66b821eb-cfc5-5167-9c91-37e6e80d6d3f" "answer-56aa150d-8b20-5d1a-b78e-808ac608f56f"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-16d0649e-68ce-5666-85e2-10cd035eb702" :answer/id #uuid "16d0649e-68ce-5666-85e2-10cd035eb702" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "-3" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-4c939ced-410b-538a-b95e-7eabbbc8766a" :answer/id #uuid "4c939ced-410b-538a-b95e-7eabbbc8766a" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "-4" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-21bd4957-61ca-515f-955c-429ec430a2c2" :answer/id #uuid "21bd4957-61ca-515f-955c-429ec430a2c2" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "-5" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-66b821eb-cfc5-5167-9c91-37e6e80d6d3f" :answer/id #uuid "66b821eb-cfc5-5167-9c91-37e6e80d6d3f" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "2" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-56aa150d-8b20-5d1a-b78e-808ac608f56f" :answer/id #uuid "56aa150d-8b20-5d1a-b78e-808ac608f56f" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "4" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "question-b15d4431-e43f-5101-96e7-ab09f0076b4a" :question/id #uuid "b15d4431-e43f-5101-96e7-ab09f0076b4a" :question/math-academy-id "q-93991" :question/problem "$$
A=[\begin{aligned}4 & 1 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrix $A$ above. Which of the following represents the corresponding bilinear form ${x}^{T}\,Ay$ in terms of the components of $x=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]$ and $y=[\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}]?$" :question/worked-solution "**Method 1**

Each entry ${a}_{ij}$ of $A$ corresponds to the term ${a}_{ij}{x}_{i}{y}_{j}$ in the expression of the bilinear form:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{T}\,Ay & =4{x}_{1}{y}_{1}+1{x}_{1}{y}_{2}+3{x}_{2}{y}_{1}+1{x}_{2}{y}_{2} \\  & =4{x}_{1}{y}_{1}+{x}_{1}{y}_{2}+3{x}_{2}{y}_{1}+{x}_{2}{y}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

**Method 2**

To write down a bilinear form in terms of vector components, we compute the following expression:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{T}\,Ay & =[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & {x}_{2}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 & 1 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & {x}_{2}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4{y}_{1}+{y}_{2} \\ 3{y}_{1}+{y}_{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & ={x}_{1}(4{y}_{1}+{y}_{2})+{x}_{2}(3{y}_{1}+{y}_{2}) \\  & =4{x}_{1}{y}_{1}+{x}_{1}{y}_{2}+3{x}_{2}{y}_{1}+{x}_{2}{y}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-43d9d476-deb7-5159-945c-bd382763aea3"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id Each entry ${a}_{ij}$ of $A$ corresponds to the term ${a}_{ij}{x}_{i}{y}_{j}$ in the expression of the bilinear form:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{T}\,Ay & =1{x}_{1}{y}_{1}+(-2){x}_{1}{y}_{2}+2{x}_{2}{y}_{1}+1{x}_{2}{y}_{2} \\  & ={x}_{1}{y}_{1}-2{x}_{1}{y}_{2}+2{x}_{2}{y}_{1}+{x}_{2}{y}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

**Method 2**

To write down a bilinear form in terms of vector components, we compute the following expression:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{T}\,Ay & =[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & {x}_{2}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & {x}_{2}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{y}_{1}-2{y}_{2} \\ 2{y}_{1}+{y}_{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & ={x}_{1}({y}_{1}-2{y}_{2})+{x}_{2}(2{y}_{1}+{y}_{2}) \\  & ={x}_{1}{y}_{1}-2{x}_{1}{y}_{2}+2{x}_{2}{y}_{1}+{x}_{2}{y}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186160832 :answer-field/correct "answer-989ea25f-37be-568e-b80b-e6e58c5da663" :answer-field/choices ["answer-eb109607-0a7d-5ec5-83c6-08f21eea7ccc" "answer-989ea25f-37be-568e-b80b-e6e58c5da663" "answer-46905384-ce8a-5ab9-af0b-2976fe3be6b4" "answer-aaeac9ef-7f69-5e21-b596-8a8eced51973" "answer-08e5bf9a-2ab7-5739-b14d-f546e211c130"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-eb109607-0a7d-5ec5-83c6-08f21eea7ccc" :answer/id #uuid "eb109607-0a7d-5ec5-83c6-08f21eea7ccc" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "{x}_{1}{y}_{1}+2{x}_{1}{y}_{2}-2{x}_{2}{y}_{1}+{x}_{2}{y}_{2}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-989ea25f-37be-568e-b80b-e6e58c5da663" :answer/id #uuid "989ea25f-37be-568e-b80b-e6e58c5da663" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "{x}_{1}{y}_{1}-2{x}_{1}{y}_{2}+2{x}_{2}{y}_{1}+{x}_{2}{y}_{2}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-46905384-ce8a-5ab9-af0b-2976fe3be6b4" :answer/id #uuid "46905384-ce8a-5ab9-af0b-2976fe3be6b4" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "{x}_{1}{y}_{1}-2{x}_{1}{y}_{2}+2{x}_{2}{y}_{1}-{x}_{2}{y}_{2}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-aaeac9ef-7f69-5e21-b596-8a8eced51973" :answer/id #uuid "aaeac9ef-7f69-5e21-b596-8a8eced51973" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "{x}_{1}{y}_{1}-{x}_{1}{y}_{2}+2{x}_{2}{y}_{1}+2{x}_{2}{y}_{2}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-08e5bf9a-2ab7-5739-b14d-f546e211c130" :answer/id #uuid "08e5bf9a-2ab7-5739-b14d-f546e211c130" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "{x}_{1}{y}_{1}-{x}_{1}{y}_{2}+{x}_{2}{y}_{1}+{x}_{2}{y}_{2}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "question-8f253585-3e9e-576c-84e8-68a00302ab3a" :question/id #uuid "8f253585-3e9e-576c-84e8-68a00302ab3a" :question/math-academy-id "q-93997" :question/problem "$$

$$
\begin{aligned}B(x,y) & =3{x}_{1}{y}_{1}+{x}_{1}{y}_{2}-5{x}_{2}{y}_{2}-2{x}_{2}{y}_{3}-2{x}_{3}{y}_{1} \\  & =3{x}_{1}{y}_{1}+1{x}_{1}{y}_{2}+0{x}_{1}{y}_{3} \\  & +\,0{x}_{2}{y}_{1}+(-5){x}_{2}{y}_{2}+(-2){x}_{2}{y}_{3} \\  & +\,(-2){x}_{3}{y}_{1}+0{x}_{3}{y}_{2}+0{x}_{3}{y}_{3}\end{aligned}

$$
[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -5 & -2 \\ -2 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].

$$

A  function 

$$
f: \Bbb R^n \to \Bbb R
$$

is a **linear form**  (or  *linear functional*) if there is a row-vector 

![](images/95/952d8832a903cf184286698e449da84d94d61cb46d984a48f33f406a42a8007a.svg)

such that for any ![](images/6b/6b756f37311a5e7f4e6cfb160a37b31d54b2ce1e29849044101dc82d49e44d21.svg) we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =ax \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{a}_{1} & {a}_{2} & ⋯ & {a}_{n}\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}] \\  & ={a}_{1}{x}_{1}+{a}_{2}{x}_{2}+…+{a}_{n}{x}_{n}.\end{aligned}
$$

For example, let $f(\mathbf{x})$ be the linear form   defined on $\Bbb R^2$ by $f(\mathbf{x}) = \mathbf{a} \mathbf{x},$ where ![](images/26/26cf6eb0836041b648c29908c8d13ae132e644ea68c772e81e011470283c3427.svg) 

Suppose we want to evaluate $f(\mathbf{x})$ at ![](images/5d/5d6ebda5e8563d23b66cdf15f4a47a1ae712510eeacbe6bcebd031534bcc841a.svg) Then, we simply substitute ![](images/6c/6c79170289a47e3ebb2a7226432938640c63ccea0d032e674d4f03967c12c8ea.svg) and obtain  

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =ax \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -2\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}\,1 \\ \,\,-1\end{aligned}] \\  & =3\cdot 1+(-2)\cdot (-1) \\  & =3+2 \\  & =5.\end{aligned}
$$" :db/ensure [:tutorial/validate]} {:db/id 17592186163234 :tutorial/content "Let $n$ be a positive integer. A  function $B: \Bbb R^n\times \Bbb R^n \to \Bbb R$ is said to be a **bilinear form** if there is an $n\times n$   matrix $A$ such that 

$$
B(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{y}) =  \mathbf{x}^T \! A\mathbf{y}, \qquad  \mathbf{x}, \mathbf{y} \in \Bbb R^n.
$$

Suppose, for example, that ![](images/e3/e3ef7815e373c266abf34e4bbba1dd9b29adf2865721afeb8bf4e3eb44b105dc.svg) To  evaluate the bilinear form $B(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y}) = \mathbf{x}^T \! A \mathbf{y}$ when ![](images/ac/ac7f10624ad2b9d0807018976526311423dc4110a98ba24f4ff7eac6760af616.svg) and ![](images/5a/5a074c9193bbe395506549cb69b1b2e84d1208211efb1008a5192989850606ce.svg) we substitute  these vectors in the above expression as follows 

$$
\begin{aligned}B(x,y) & ={x}^{T}\,Ay \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 3 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}7 & 10\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

 

To write down our bilinear form $B(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y})$ above in terms of vector components 

![](images/c4/c47fc6c2d7df7ced599a643531bc19656c7c62915930583089df641e493680e5.svg)

we proceed as follows:  

$$
\begin{aligned}B(x,y) & ={x}^{T}\,Ay \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & {x}_{2}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 3 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & {x}_{2}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{y}_{1}+2{y}_{2} \\ 3{y}_{1}+4{y}_{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & ={x}_{1}({y}_{1}+2{y}_{2})+{x}_{2}(3{y}_{1}+4{y}_{2}) \\  & ={x}_{1}{y}_{1}+2{x}_{1}{y}_{2}+3{x}_{2}{y}_{1}+4{x}_{2}{y}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$" :db/ensure [:tutorial/validate]} {:db/id 17592186162217 :activity/expected-seconds 540.0 :db/ensure [:activity/validate]}]

["question-b15d4431-e43f-5101-96e7-ab09f0076b4a" :question/math-academy-id "q-93991"] ["question-b15d4431-e43f-5101-96e7-ab09f0076b4a" :question/problem "$$
A=[\begin{aligned}4 & 1 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrix $A$ above. Which of the following represents the corresponding bilinear form ${x}^{T}\,Ay$ in terms of the components of $x=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]$ and $y=[\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}]?$"] ["question-b15d4431-e43f-5101-96e7-ab09f0076b4a" :question/worked-solution "**Method 1**

Each entry ${a}_{ij}$ of $A$ corresponds to the term ${a}_{ij}{x}_{i}{y}_{j}$ in the expression of the bilinear form:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{T}\,Ay & =4{x}_{1}{y}_{1}+1{x}_{1}{y}_{2}+3{x}_{2}{y}_{1}+1{x}_{2}{y}_{2} \\  & =4{x}_{1}{y}_{1}+{x}_{1}{y}_{2}+3{x}_{2}{y}_{1}+{x}_{2}{y}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

**Method 2**

A=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}]
$$

Each entry ${a}_{ij}$ of $A$ corresponds to the term ${a}_{ij}{x}_{i}{y}_{j}$ in the expression of the bilinear form:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{T}\,Ay & =(-2){x}_{1}{y}_{1}+1{x}_{1}{y}_{2}+(-1){x}_{2}{y}_{1}+3{x}_{2}{y}_{2} \\  & =-2{x}_{1}{y}_{1}+{x}_{1}{y}_{2}-{x}_{2}{y}_{1}+3{x}_{2}{y}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

**Method 2**

To write down a bilinear form in terms of vector components, we compute the following expression:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{T}\,Ay & =[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & {x}_{2}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & {x}_{2}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-2{y}_{1}+{y}_{2} \\ -{y}_{1}+3{y}_{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & ={x}_{1}(-2{y}_{1}+{y}_{2})+{x}_{2}(-{y}_{1}+3{y}_{2}) \\  & =-2{x}_{1}{y}_{1}+{x}_{1}{y}_{2}-{x}_{2}{y}_{1}+3{x}_{2}{y}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$"} {:db/id 17592186357614 :question/id #uuid "45479840-98ff-5a0a-8836-361250ff785d" :question/math-academy-id "q-93995"} {:db/id 17592186357615 :question/id #uuid What is the value of $a+b+c?$

$$
[\begin{aligned}a & 0 & 0 \\ b & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & c & 2\end{aligned}]
$$" :question/worked-solution "Each term $a_{ij}x_i y_j$ in the expression of the bilinear form corresponds to the entry $a_{ij}$ of the matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned}B(x,y) & =2{x}_{1}{y}_{1}+2{x}_{2}{y}_{1}-{x}_{3}{y}_{2}+2{x}_{3}{y}_{3} \\  & =2{x}_{1}{y}_{1}+0{x}_{1}{y}_{2}+0{x}_{1}{y}_{3} \\  & +\,2{x}_{2}{y}_{1}+0{x}_{2}{y}_{2}+0{x}_{2}{y}_{3} \\  & +\,0{x}_{3}{y}_{1}+(-1){x}_{3}{y}_{2}+2{x}_{3}{y}_{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, the corresponding matrix of the bilinear form is

![](images/24/24b1e29dccdff51c2ca2c7780a8a5dfcf9c74ed91d48afdde8a14c5127f89ce1.png)

Therefore, $a=2,$ $b=2,$ and $c=-1.$ Finally,

A  function 

$$
f: \Bbb R^n \to \Bbb R
$$

is a **linear form**  (or  *linear functional*) if there is a row-vector 

$$
[\begin{aligned}{a}_{1} & {a}_{2} & ⋯ & {a}_{n}\end{aligned}]
$$

such that for any $[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]$ we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =ax \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{a}_{1} & {a}_{2} & ⋯ & {a}_{n}\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}] \\  & ={a}_{1}{x}_{1}+{a}_{2}{x}_{2}+…+{a}_{n}{x}_{n}.\end{aligned}
$$

For example, let $f(\mathbf{x})$ be the linear form   defined on $\Bbb R^2$ by $f(\mathbf{x}) = \mathbf{a} \mathbf{x},$ where $[\begin{aligned}3 & -2\end{aligned}]$ 

Suppose we want to evaluate $f(\mathbf{x})$ at $[\begin{aligned}\,1 \\ \,\,-1\end{aligned}]$ Then, we simply substitute $[\begin{aligned}\,1 \\ \,\,-1\end{aligned}]$ and obtain  

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =ax \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -2\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}\,1 \\ \,\,-1\end{aligned}] \\  & =3\cdot 1+(-2)\cdot (-1) \\  & =3+2 \\  & =5.\end{aligned}
$$" :tutorial/id #uuid "a0cf8344-4180-5121-8429-bf2232ea1c94" :tutorial/math-academy-id 4883 :tutorial/title "Introduction"} :step/id #uuid "10801c67-6977-5b0e-8ebd-4c3a8edd48f7" :step/math-academy-id 30534 :step/next {:db/id 17592186162860}} {:db/id 17592186162860 :step/content {:db/id 17592186161980 :knowledge-point/canonical-example {:db/id 17592186161772 :question/id #uuid "59ea7ebb-5b69-5551-a5b9-c286e2730881" :question/math-academy-id "e-8160"} :knowledge-point/id #uuid "5b58f4ff-b6ed-5df6-b04f-137e285d5460" :knowledge-point/key-prerequisites [{:db/id 17592186048652} {:db/id 17592186048954}] :knowledge-point/questions [{:db/id 17592186162587} {:db/id 17592186162611} {:db/id 17592186272163} {:db/id 17592186272164} {:db/id 17592186357595} {:db/id 17592186357603} {:db/id 17592186357604}] :knowledge-point/title "Evaluating a Linear Form"} :step/id #uuid "a5a71a2d-8697-5b95-99ea-19befec73017" :step/math-academy-id 30561 :step/next {:db/id 17592186162861}} {:db/id 17592186162861 :step/content {:db/id 17592186163234 :tutorial/content "Let $n$ be a positive integer. $$
B(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{y}) =  \mathbf{x}^T \! A\mathbf{y}, \qquad  \mathbf{x}, \mathbf{y} \in \Bbb R^n.
$$

Suppose, for example, that $[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 3 & 4\end{aligned}]$ To  evaluate the bilinear form $B(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y}) = \mathbf{x}^T \! A \mathbf{y}$ when $[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]$ and $[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ we substitute  these vectors in the above expression as follows

17592186046941 17592186045417] [17592186046658 1005 17592186046975 17592186045417] [17592186046658 1007 "Mathematics for Machine Learning" 17592186045417] [17592186046658 1008 "Our Mathematics for Machine Learning course provides a comprehensive foundation of the essential mathematical tools required to study modern machine learning.
This course is divided into three main categories: linear algebra, multivariable calculus, and probability & statistics. The linear algebra section covers crucial machine learning fundamentals such as matrices, vector spaces, diagonalization, projections, singular value decomposition, and regression, as well as dimensionality reduction techniques such as principal component analysis. The multivariable calculus section develops the tools needed for optimization and learning algorithms, including vector and matrix calculus. Finally, the probability and statistics section covers random variables, point estimation, maximum likelihood estimation, and confidence intervals.
On completing this course, students will be well-prepared for a university-level machine learning course that tackles concepts such as gradient descent, neural networks, backpropagation, support vector machines, naive Bayes classifiers, and Gaussian mixture models." 17592186045417] [17592186046658 1009 "The course begins with foundational topics in set theory and logic. Students develop a precise mathematical language for describing sets, functions, and predicates, and are introduced to key ideas such as supremum and infimum, as well as argmax and argmin notation. Logical reasoning and Boolean functions are also studied, providing important conceptual motivation for understanding the expressive limitations of some simple machine learning models, such as why certain functions (e.g. XOR) cannot be represented by a single-layer neural network.
Students then explore matrices in-depth. They study Gaussian elimination, solve systems of equations, learn about determinants and their properties, and compute inverse matrices. These tools form the computational backbone of many machine learning algorithms.
As part of this course, students perform a deep dive into vector spaces, exploring linear independence, subspaces, bases, dimension, rank, and nullity. They also study operations such as the Hadamard product, which appears naturally in element-wise computations in neural networks. Students generalize key concepts to abstract vector spaces and inner product spaces, and study orthogonality, projections, and the Gram–Schmidt process.
Students will learn how to find eigenvectors of a matrix, compute matrix diagonalizations, and extend these ideas to orthogonal diagonalization of symmetric matrices. These techniques underpin dimensionality reduction methods and are central to understanding the structure of data.
The course then develops key applications of linear algebra in machine learning. Students study singular value decomposition and its relationship to principal component analysis, and learn how these tools are used for dimensionality reduction, feature extraction, and identifying structure in high-dimensional datasets. Linear least-squares problems and regression techniques are also studied as foundational methods for fitting models to data.
A solid grasp of multivariable calculus is essential for understanding modern machine learning algorithms. In this course, students become well-versed in partial derivatives and gradient vectors (used in gradient-based optimization), the multivariable chain rule (essential for backpropagation), and vector-valued functions. Students extend differentiation to maps between multi-dimensional vector spaces and develop the tools of vector and matrix calculus used to compute gradients of loss functions in neural networks.
Students also study optimization of multivariable functions, including critical points, second derivative tests, and constrained optimization using Lagrange multipliers. These techniques form the mathematical foundation of algorithms such as support vector machines and constrained optimization problems in machine learning.
Students work with standard multivariable surfaces to build intuition for loss surfaces, and study double integrals as a tool for understanding continuous probability distributions.
On the probability and statistics side, students study discrete and continuous random variables, including probability density functions, cumulative distribution functions, transformations, expectation, moments, variance, and Bayes' theorem. Important probability distributions are explored in detail.
Students extend their understanding to joint, marginal, and conditional distributions, as well as sums and products of random variables. Topics such as covariance, correlation, and multivariate normal distributions are introduced, which are essential in probabilistic modeling.
The course concludes with parametric inference, focusing on point estimation, maximum likelihood estimation, and confidence intervals, which form the statistical foundation for many machine learning
